title: Autism Collaboration, Accountability, Research, Education, and Support Act of 2019
official_summary:
Autism Collaboration, Accountability, Research, Education, and Support Act of 2019 or the Autism CARES Act of 2019

This bill reauthorizes through FY2024 and revises several programs and activities relating to autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Specifically, the bill reauthorizes provisions relating to (1) expanded ASD research at the National Institutes of Health; (2) the collection of state-level ASD data by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; (3) ASD education, early detection, and intervention activities supported by the Health Resources and Services Administration; and (4) the Interagency Autism Coordinating Committee.

The bill also generally revises the scope of such programs and activities to (1) encompass ASD individuals of all ages, rather than only youth; (2) focus funding on programs in areas with a shortage of personal health services; and (3) reduce health-outcome disparities across diverse populations.

summary.headline: Congress extended federal autism research, data collection, and support programs through 2024 and widened them to cover people of all ages.
summary.what_it_does: This law renews several federal autism programs through fiscal year 2024. It covers research at the National Institutes of Health, state autism data collection by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and education and early detection work supported by the Health Resources and Services Administration. It also continues the Interagency Autism Coordinating Committee. The programs now serve autistic people of every age instead of only children, and funding is directed toward areas with shortages of health services and toward reducing health gaps among different populations.

who_it_affects.how: Federal autism programs now cover adults as well as children rather than only youth.

who_it_affects.group: Families and caregivers of autistic people
who_it_affects.how: They may find more federally supported education, early detection, and intervention services, especially in areas with few health providers.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of areas with shortages of personal health services
who_it_affects.how: Federal autism funding is directed toward these areas.
They may continue to receive federal support for collecting state-level autism data through the CDC.
NIH autism research programs are reauthorized through fiscal year 2024.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted September 30, 2019, with the reauthorized programs running through fiscal year 2024.
